Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are making their way out in the middle now. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Perera are the two openers for Sri Lanka. Netherlands going with the same tactics of starting with spin as Aryan Dutt is ready to bowl now. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the target for Sri Lanka is 263. Can they chase it down and get their first win of the tournament or will the Netherlands make it two wins in a row? An exciting second half is up on the cards. Do join us in a bit for the second innings.

Sybrand Engelbrecht, the top-scorer for Netherlands is up for a quick chat.  He says that he is happy with his knock and thinks that this is a competitive total. Credits Logan van Beek for his batting as well and says that the pitch is a bit tricky. Tells that there is some turn but they need to bowl really well to defend this one. Mentions that it was important to bat deep and they managed to do that so he is happy with it. End by saying they are up for the challenge.

Kasun Rajitha started nicely with the ball and removed the top three batters in his opening spell. He came back at the end and picked up the crucial wicket of van Beek to end with a 4-fer. Dilshan Madhushanka carried on his fine form and snapped 4 for 49 in his yet another impressive outing with the ball. Theekshana picked up a wicket in the middle. Sri Lanka have done decently well but will be unhappy to let things slip in the second half of the innings. They would have liked to dismiss the Netherlands below 200 but will now have to chase 263.

A brilliant recovery from the Netherlands gets them to a reasonable score of 262 in their allotted overs. Opting to bat first, the Dutch were reeling at 91 for 6 in the 23rd over and were in all sorts of trouble. They were in danger of not batting out their overs but Sybrand Engelbrecht and Logan van Beek got together and added a brilliant 130 for the seventh wicket. The duo absorbed the pressure and went about ticking the score early on. Once set, the batters took charge and got boundaries at will. Engelbrecht made an outstanding 70 off 82 while Logan van Beek supported him well and scored a well-made 59 off 75. The lower order got some handy runs at the backend and took their side over 260.

NO BALL AND RUN OUT! A chaotic end to the innings! This is full and around off, Paul van Meekeren looks to reverse-scoop it but misses and looks at the keeper. However, his partner sets off for the run and is already halfway through when Paul van Meekeren starts to run, Kusal Mendis throws it to the bowler where Dilshan Madushanka collects it and takes a couple of steps towards the stump and underarms the ball to break it with the batter nowhere near the creases. The umpire signals a No Ball for overstepping but the run out stands and Netherlands misses out on a Free Hit on the last ball. The Dutch finish on 262!

We are moments away from the start of the match but before that, both sets of players line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's first followed by the national anthem of Netherlands.

Kusal Mendis, the captain of Sri Lanka says that they have three injuries which is always a concern but everyone in the squad is quality. Tells that their opening pair batted well in the previous game and in general their batters have been good in the last couple of matches. Says if their bowling also improves, they could be better. Mentions he is enjoying his role as a batter and the captaincy as well.

Scott Edwards, the skipper of Netherlands says that they will bat first. He says that the pitch looks good and batting seems a good option. States that they have areas to work upon and they are here to win and compete. Adds that they have quality spinners and quicks which made the job easy for him. Closes by saying that there are no changes to the lineup.

TOSS - Netherlands have won the toss and they will BAT first.

Sri Lanka, on the other hand, have lost all three games so far and are yet to get off the mark in the season. The team hasn’t performed to its potential and have been marred by injuries before the World Cup and even during the mega event. In their last game against Australia, the Lankans got off to a fine start with the openers putting 125 for the opening wicket. The middle and lower order crumbled and were bundled out for a below-par 209. Australia chased it with ease and thumped Sri Lanka by a massive margin. Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Perera, and Kusal Mendis have been in good form so far in the tournament while Charith Asalanka has also played important knocks in the middle order. Dilshan Madhushanka has been their most impressive bowler on show with 7 wickets in three games and has troubled the batters with his swing. Sri Lanka will need to step up as a team if they are to beat the in-form Netherlands. A fascinating contest is up on the cards. Stick around as we bring the toss and team news shortly.

The Netherlands registered a sensational win by defeating the fancied South Africa and caused a major upset in the tournament. Batting first in a rain-affected game, the Dutch made a competitive score of 245 in 43 overs on the back of a brilliant knock from their skipper Scott Edwards. The bowlers turned up and dismissed South Africa for 207, winning the game by 38 runs. The Dutch have a well-rounded score with Max O’Dowd and Vikramjit Singh doing well at the top while Colin Ackermann, Teja Nidamanuru, and Scott Edwards form up the middle order.
